author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected on a form at that visit's own URL, under the booking rules. The correction changes that visit in place and returns the reader to the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit is requested, then the visit form is shown holding that visit's current date and description
given a description and a date later than today, when POST to the same URL is submitted, then that visit carries the new values and the response redirects to the owner's record
given an accepted correction, when the pet's visits are read, then the pet has the same number of visits as before
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then the form is shown again, the description is named, and the stored visit is unchanged
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then the form is shown again, the date is named, and the stored visit is unchanged
edge case 3: opening or submitting a correction for a visit that does not exist, or that does not belong to the named pet, is refused
edge case 4: a visit whose date has passed opens with that date, and a correction to it is accepted only with a date later than today
non_goals: a link or any other entry point to the correction form on the owner's record (NG-10)
correcting anything on a visit other than its date and description
a confirmation message for an accepted correction, or new form wording (open question in docs/prd.md)
notes: Owner-fixed surface, intake line 1 request: "Reuse the existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit` model attribute." Narrowest-reading choices, per the same request, recorded as Open Questions in docs/prd.md: a past visit needs a future date to be corrected; the form keeps the booking wording and no confirmation is required. The refusal in edge case 3 is left to design, consistent with Visits edge case 1. Non-goal changes: NG-5 narrowed, NG-10 added, docs/adr/2026-10-31-non-goal-visit-correction.md added, and the 2026-08-08 ADR's status amended. docs/adr/README.md is outside this agent's write scope: system-design-expert adds the index row for the new ADR. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the owner aggregate and feature package unchanged: VisitController resolves owner, pet, and visit per request, and OwnerRepository cascade is the write (system-design § Contracts, invariants paragraph). Adjustments: one lookup on Pet, one Form validator (catalog row in force, PetValidator is the precedent), one correction branch in the existing @ModelAttribute, and one § Scale and Load row. No new pattern, no ADR. Basis is grep and source reading; the IDE oracle is not connected. Correction replaces no recorded design decision: NG-5 was narrowed by the owner, line 3 scope_overrides.
integration_points: Model attribute: loadPetWithVisit gains @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId, the PetController.findPet precedent. With a visitId it returns the pet's stored visit and adds nothing; without one it keeps today's new Visit plus pet.addVisit. The method runs before every handler, so the refusal covers GET and POST in one place.

Lookup: Pet gains Optional<Visit> findVisit(Integer id) (architecture-principles § Java Idioms, Optional over null checks). The controller calls orElseThrow with IllegalArgumentException, the same refusal as a missing pet, satisfying edge case 3 and consistent with Visits edge case 1. The message carries identifiers only (security-principles, secret disclosure row).

Binding, entry points GET and POST .../visits/{visitId}/edit: target is the Visit model attribute, a persisted type behind an allow-list. Add @InitBinder("visit") with setAllowedFields("date", "description"); the existing id and *.id disallow stays. The POST handler declares @ModelAttribute(binding = false) Owner owner: Owner is never a binding target on this route.

Date rule: VisitValidator (Form validator row) is the rule's single home. Register it in @InitBinder("visit") with addValidators, never setValidator, which would drop @NotBlank. Construct it per binder with today's date as a constructor argument (architecture-principles design principle 3). Remove the check from processNewVisitForm. Keep the error code typeMismatch.visitDate, which the existing test asserts. Skip the date rule when date already has a binding error.

Success path: bind onto the stored visit, then owners.save(owner); never owner.addVisit. Redirect to redirect:/owners/{ownerId}. No flash attribute: the prd-entry excludes a confirmation, and the booking flash text says booked.

Template: rename the Previous Visits loop variable to previous and filter with !previous['new'] and previous.id != visit.id. Booking output is unchanged. No other template change: the heading and button keep the booking wording per prd-entry non_goals, and the form posts to its own URL.
Doubles, transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness (testing-principles § Mocking Policy).

Doubles, repository: real OwnerRepository on H2 for every test that asserts stored state or visit count, in VisitCorrectionIntegrationTests (@SpringBootTest, @AutoConfigureMockMvc): theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitAndRedirectToTheOwnerRecord, theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddAVisitToThePet, theRefusedVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveTheStoredVisitUnchanged. Do not annotate that class @Transactional: a test transaction makes loaded entities managed, so a refused bind would flush and the test would stop modelling production. Each test creates its own visit through the repository and re-reads through findById.

Doubles, repository in VisitControllerTests: the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository stays for the form and refusal tests only. Reason: the class is a @WebMvcTest slice with no JPA context, and JpaRepository is too wide for a hand-written double. Unhandled refusals surface in MockMvc as a thrown ServletException with the IllegalArgumentException as cause.
Doubles, validator: VisitValidatorTests uses no double and a fixed today value, in the PetValidatorTests shape.

findings.description: Pet.findVisit is a new public seam with its own decision (visit found by id, or empty), and docs/system-design.md:125 records it as a hand-written linear scan of a pet's visits. Its only coverage is through framework-booted tests: VisitControllerTests (WebMvcTest) and VisitCorrectionIntegrationTests (SpringBootTest). `grep -F -e findVisit -- src/test` finds one hit, a helper call at VisitCorrectionIntegrationTests.java:150, and no direct test. The pyramid question is whether it could be tested without the framework, and here it can. A change that broke the scan for a pet with several visits, for an unsaved visit whose id is null, or for a pet with none would only surface through a controller exception path. Add a plain unit test in a new PetTests: a pet with no visits returns empty, a matching id among several visits returns that visit, a non-matching id returns empty, and a pet holding an unsaved (null-id) visit still finds the saved one. Keep the controller tests' single representative missing-visit and other-pet's-visit path.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: A description over 255 characters is unresolved on the new write route. Visit.java declares only `@NotBlank` on description, while h2/schema.sql:62 reads `description VARCHAR(255)`, so such a post should fail at the database as a 500 rather than a form refusal on H2 and MySQL. This was reasoned from the code and not exercised here. Booking has the same gap and the correction route extends it. It fails closed, since the stored row stays unchanged. No `server.error` setting exists in src/main/resources (grep of application*.properties), and devtools is developmentOnly (build.gradle:50 `developmentOnly 'org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-devtools'`). Any failure text on the page is therefore expected only in development runs, and that default was not verified here. A length rule would change booking too, so it needs its own decision, which this review could not find recorded beyond the design note leaving it open.
approved_aspects: Mass assignment: the correction route binds only date and description. VisitController.java:55 `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id");` and :61 `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description");` both apply to the `visit` attribute, and :140 `@ModelAttribute(binding = false) Owner owner` keeps Owner unbound, so the save at :146 carries no request-supplied owner field. The bound-Owner weakness stays on the booking handler at :118 and the pet form handlers, the existing Known Defect, and this change does not extend it.

Object-level reach: every GET and POST re-resolves the visit through its URL parents. :84 `Pet pet = owner.getPet(petId);`, then :93 `return pet.findVisit(visitId)`, refusing with IllegalArgumentException before binding. Pet.findVisit scans only that pet's visits, so an identifier from another pet or owner cannot be reached and no earlier request is trusted. The absence of authentication is the standing baseline in docs/security-principles.md; the threat-model row at system-design.md:190 `Correcting another pet's visit` records the new route's exposure.

No weakened check: the date test removed from processNewVisitForm is replaced by an equal control, not a weaker one. VisitValidator keeps `date != null && !date.isAfter(this.today)` and :66 `dataBinder.addValidators(new VisitValidator(LocalDate.now()));` adds to bean validation rather than replacing it. @Valid is present on both POST handlers (:118, :140). The validator is built per binder, so the singleton controller holds no mutable state and today is not frozen at startup. The allow-list at :61 also narrows booking's binding.

Missing-date refusal: :64 `dataBinder.setRequiredFields("date");` applies only when visitId is present, and booking keeps its recorded null-date behavior as the PRD edge case states. From my reading of Spring's binder order, the `_date` and `!date` marker parameters are expanded before the required check, so they should not slip a null past it. That ordering is recalled, not exercised in this review or read from the Spring source; `date.year`-style nested paths are outside the exact allow-list.

Refused corrections do not persist: application.properties:11 `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` leaves the owner graph detached, and the error branch at :142 returns before the only save at :146, so rejected values never reach the database.

Output and injection: the template change uses th:text only, and `grep -rn -F -e th:utext -e '__${' src/main/resources/templates` shows no th:utext. The preprocessing hits use entity ids or fragment parameters fixed by templates, none of them request text. A rejected date or description is echoed through th:field and th:errors, which escape. The redirect is the fixed template `redirect:/owners/{ownerId}` with an int path variable, so it is not an open redirect. The diff adds no query text, file, process, or deserialization sink and no log call. The new exception message at :95 carries integer ids only, which is safe for the error page that renders exception messages.

Secrets: a case-insensitive grep of the src/main and src/test diff for password, secret, token, api key, and credential returned no added line, so the production and test code adds no credential. Untracked files were read directly, not grepped.

Supply chain: `git status --short build.gradle gradle/ settings.gradle` printed nothing, so no dependency changed. No NVD match ran, the standing gap in docs/security-principles.md; `grep -n -F -e dependencycheck -e dependencyCheck build.gradle` had no hits. The `dependencies` output resolves Spring Boot 4.1.2 and Jackson 3.1.7 (tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind).
`./gradlew test` ran and reported BUILD SUCCESSFUL with all tasks up-to-date, so it confirms the cached result for this tree rather than a fresh execution.
Process: my first tool calls were two read-only log lookups, so `dispatch-start` was appended third rather than first. No review work preceded it.

The rule is stateless and receives today as a constructor argument, and VisitController builds it per binder via `new VisitValidator(LocalDate.now())`. The lookup is Pet.findVisit on the aggregate that owns the visits, not an inline controller scan. The stream scan fits the system-design.md Scale and Load row `One pet's visits` (`Unrecorded, treated as bounded`, Form `Linear scan`), so the simplest form stands.
